messages.content: Predict an actual human participant's choice. This is a four-member public goods experiment with three computer players, not people; their choices are independently and randomly selected from earlier experiment decisions, your choice cannot affect their algorithm, and only you receive money. Each member has 20 MU. A contribution c is an integer 0–20 MU;20-c stays private. Own game earnings=20-c+0.5*(c+the sum of the three others' contributions). No communication; decisions are anonymous. A 10 RMB show-up fee is retained;100 MU=40 RMB, and earnings are added and paid at the end. You previously received the experiment instructions and control questions, and answered the payoff-maximization question. Neither other players' realized choices nor game payoff feedback has been shown before this contribution. Commit one joint contribution schedule for the hypothetical other-member mean grid[0,5,10,15,20] MU. All entries are on one screen with one confirmation. One situation is randomly selected to calculate payoff. Each entry has a fresh alternative 20 MU budget: no cross-entry sum or monotonicity restriction. The hypothetical grid is not observed realized peer behavior. Output only a text JSON array of 5 integer contributions 0–20 in that order. Participant attributes are self-reported stable age/major/household income/expenses, collected at the end but personally known earlier; they are not current game outcomes. major_code 1–7 respectively means humanities and social science, science, engineering, medicine, agriculture, economics and management, other. monthly_household_income_code and monthly_expenses_code 1–4 mean below 1000, 1000–3000, 3000–5000, above 5000 RMB; household income is per capita. own_prior_payoff_maximization_answer_MU is your earlier answer to the hypothetical question about maximizing own benefit when others total 30 MU, not a contribution in the current game.

Predict an actual human participant's choice. This is a four-member public goods experiment with three computer players, not people; their choices are independently and randomly selected from earlier experiment decisions, your choice cannot affect their algorithm, and only you receive money. Each member has 20 MU. A contribution c is an integer 0–20 MU;20-c stays private. Own game earnings=20-c+0.5*(c+the sum of the three others' contributions). No communication; decisions are anonymous. A 10 RMB show-up fee is retained;100 MU=40 RMB, and earnings are added and paid at the end. You previously received the experiment instructions and control questions, and answered the payoff-maximization question. Neither other players' realized choices nor game payoff feedback has been shown before this contribution. Now make one unconditional, one-round contribution without knowing the other three current contributions. This is a separate submission after your earlier schedule. Output only the integer 0–20 of your contribution, without explanation. Participant attributes are self-reported stable age/major/household income/expenses, collected at the end but personally known earlier; they are not current game outcomes. major_code 1–7 respectively means humanities and social science, science, engineering, medicine, agriculture, economics and management, other. monthly_household_income_code and monthly_expenses_code 1–4 mean below 1000, 1000–3000, 3000–5000, above 5000 RMB; household income is per capita. own_prior_payoff_maximization_answer_MU is your earlier answer to the hypothetical question about maximizing own benefit when others total 30 MU, not a contribution in the current game. own_prior_schedule_MU gives your already submitted schedule on the stated grid.

Predict an actual human participant's choice. The earlier four-member public goods experiment was with three computer players, not people; their choices are independently and randomly selected from earlier experiment decisions, your choice cannot affect their algorithm, and only you receive money. Each member has 20 MU. A contribution c is an integer 0–20 MU;20-c stays private. Own game earnings=20-c+0.5*(c+the sum of the three others' contributions). No communication; decisions are anonymous. A 10 RMB show-up fee is retained;100 MU=40 RMB, and earnings are added and paid at the end. You previously received the experiment instructions and control questions, and answered the payoff-maximization question. Neither other players' realized choices nor game payoff feedback has been shown before this contribution. The PGG contribution stages are over. Now choose social-appropriateness ratings in an incentivized coordination game: match what most other participants in this experiment rate each action. One possible action is drawn from each of six situation categories; a majority match pays 10 MU for that category, otherwise 0; maximum 60 MU. No feedback about others' ratings has been shown. The current table contains Person A's five possible contributions 0,5,10,15,20 MU, in that order. current_hypothetical_other_mean_MU=null means their contributions are unknown to Person A; a number is the hypothetical mean known to Person A. For each, select 1=very socially inappropriate,2=inappropriate,3=somewhat inappropriate,4=somewhat appropriate,5=appropriate,6=very appropriate. Ratings are simultaneously confirmed as one five-component submission. Output only a text JSON array of five integers 1–6 in the stated order. These ratings do not implement a PGG contribution. Participant attributes are self-reported stable age/major/household income/expenses, collected at the end but personally known earlier; they are not current game outcomes. major_code 1–7 respectively means humanities and social science, science, engineering, medicine, agriculture, economics and management, other. monthly_household_income_code and monthly_expenses_code 1–4 mean below 1000, 1000–3000, 3000–5000, above 5000 RMB; household income is per capita. own_prior_payoff_maximization_answer_MU is your earlier answer to the hypothetical question about maximizing own benefit when others total 30 MU, not a contribution in the current game. own_prior_schedule_MU gives your already submitted schedule on the stated grid. partner_type describes the earlier PGG. own_prior_unconditional_contribution_MU is your earlier scalar PGG submission; previous_norm_tables contains only your already submitted norm tables.
